family: basic validation (emails by simple rules, passwords, ISBN checksums, brackets balanced)
spec: Validate whether the double-quote characters (") in a string s are properly paired. Scanning left to right, each " toggles between an outside-quotes and inside-quotes state, starting outside. Return True if the string ends in the outside-quotes state, meaning there is an even number of " characters in total; otherwise return False. All other characters are irrelevant.
reference:
def is_valid_double_quote_pairs(s):
    return s.count('"') % 2 == 0

spec: Validate whether the single-quote characters (') in a string s are properly paired. Scanning left to right, each ' toggles between an outside-quotes and inside-quotes state, starting outside. Return True if the string ends in the outside-quotes state, meaning there is an even number of ' characters in total; otherwise return False. All other characters are irrelevant.
reference:
def is_valid_single_quote_pairs(s):
    return s.count("'") % 2 == 0

family: basic validation (emails by simple rules, passwords, ISBN checksums, brackets balanced)
spec: Validate whether a string is a well-formed single-quoted string literal. It must start with a single-quote (') and end with a single-quote, with at least those two characters present. Inside the literal, a backslash always starts an escape sequence and must be followed immediately by either another backslash or a single-quote (any other character after a backslash, or a backslash at the very end, is invalid); any single-quote that is not immediately preceded by an unescaped backslash must not appear except as the final closing quote. Return False if any of these rules is violated.

family: basic validation (emails by simple rules, passwords, ISBN checksums, brackets balanced)
spec: Validate whether a string is a well-formed double-quoted string literal with escapes. It must start and end with a double-quote (") with at least those two characters present. Inside the literal, the only allowed escape sequences are \\\\ (backslash), \\" (double-quote), \\n (newline) and \\t (tab); a backslash followed by anything else, or a backslash at the very end, is invalid, and an unescaped double-quote may not appear except as the final closing quote. Return False if any rule is violated.

Return True if every opening tag has a matching closing tag with the same word, properly nested in the correct order (like balanced brackets), and there is no leftover text between or outside tags; otherwise return False.

Return True if every opening tag has a matching closing tag with the same word, properly nested in the correct order, and there is no text outside of tags; otherwise return False.

family: basic validation (emails by simple rules, passwords, ISBN checksums, brackets balanced)
spec: Validate a string of simplified tags where each tag is either a matched pair opening '<word>' ... closing '</word>' (word is one or more lowercase letters, properly nested) or a self-closing tag '<word/>'. No other text is allowed anywhere. Return True if the whole string decomposes into such tags with correct nesting; otherwise return False.

family: basic validation (emails by simple rules, passwords, ISBN checksums, brackets balanced)
spec: Validate a Sudoku column given as a list of exactly 9 integers where 0 represents an empty cell. Every non-zero value must be between 1 and 9 inclusive, and no non-zero value may repeat within the column. Return False if the list is not length 9, contains an out-of-range value, or has a duplicate non-zero value.

family: basic validation (emails by simple rules, passwords, ISBN checksums, brackets balanced)
spec: Validate a full Sudoku board given as a list of 9 lists of 9 integers (0 represents empty). Every non-zero value must be 1-9. Return True only if every row, every column, and every one of the nine non-overlapping 3x3 boxes contains no repeated non-zero value; the board need not be fully filled in. Return False if the shape is wrong, a value is out of range, or any row, column or box has a duplicate non-zero value.
visible_tests: assert is_valid_sudoku_full_board([[0]*9 for _ in range(9)]) == True
hidden_tests: assert is_valid_sudoku_full_board([[0]*9 for _ in range(8)]) == False
assert is_valid_sudoku_full_board([[0]*9 for _ in range(9)]) == True

family: basic validation (emails by simple rules, passwords, ISBN checksums, brackets balanced)
spec: Validate the main diagonal of a square Sudoku-style board given as a list of 9 lists of 9 integers (0 represents empty). Look only at the 9 cells where the row index equals the column index. Every non-zero value among those cells must be between 1 and 9 inclusive, and no non-zero value may repeat. Return False if the board is not 9x9, a diagonal value is out of range, or a diagonal value repeats.
visible_tests: assert is_valid_sudoku_diagonal([[0]*9 for _ in range(9)]) == True
assert is_valid_sudoku_diagonal([[1]*9 for _ in range(9)]) == False
hidden_tests: assert is_valid_sudoku_diagonal([[0]*9 for _ in range(8)]) == False
assert is_valid_sudoku_diagonal([[(i+1) if j==i else 0 for j in range(9)] for i in range(9)]) == True
assert is_valid_sudoku_diagonal([[0]*9 for _ in range(8)]+[[0]*8+[9]]) == True
assert is_valid_sudoku_diagonal([[1 if j==i else 0 for j in range(9)] for i in range(9)]) == False
assert is_valid_sudoku_diagonal([[0]*9 for _ in range(8)]+[[0]*8]) == False
assert is_valid_sudoku_diagonal([[0]*10]+[[0]*9 for _ in range(8)]) == False
assert is_valid_sudoku_diagonal([[7 if j==i else 3 for j in range(9)] for i in range(9)]) == False
assert is_valid_sudoku_diagonal([[9 if (i,j)==(8,8) else 0 for j in range(9)] for i in range(9)]) == True

family: basic validation (emails by simple rules, passwords, ISBN checksums, brackets balanced)
spec: Validate whether a list of numbers is strictly monotonically increasing: every element must be strictly greater than the one before it. A list with fewer than 2 elements is considered strictly increasing (True). Return False if any element is not greater than its predecessor.
reference:
def is_monotonic_increasing(seq):
    return all(seq[i] < seq[i+1] for i in range(len(seq) - 1))
